desc: THE single blocker for a multi-core daily driver on t6040. Under SMP, the first userspace process after switch_root SIGSEGVs with copy_page -> copy_user_highpage -> do_wp_page, i.e. copy-on-write page copying corrupts or writes a page it must not. Supersedes the narrow unpack_to_rootfs framing in 121: the SAME fault hits ordinary CoW with a 1.8 MB initramfs and no unpack pressure. EVIDENCE: maxcpus=1 -> zero call traces, clean system, repeatedly; maxcpus=4 -> SIGSEGV (exitcode 0x0000000b) + panic; maxcpus=3 and 5 -> hang; maxcpus=4 booted the 99 MB i3 image once. Non-monotonic => a RACE whose window widens with the amount of page copying. REPRODUCER (fast, reliable, no enrollment): boot initramfs-sdroot.cpio.gz with EXTRA_BOOTARGS='maxcpus=N console=ttydc0 sdroot.shell' -- switch_root execs a bare shell, so the very first userspace CoW either survives or panics within ~4 s. Faulting instruction was a8300c02 (stp, a store). LINES OF ATTACK, cheapest first: (1) find the maxcpus threshold precisely with the reproducer (2 vs 3) since 2 may be usable and is untested; (2) suspect cache/TLB maintenance on this core generation -- Everest/Sawtooth mixed clusters, check whether flush_dcache_page / __sync_icache_dcache / the CoW copy path needs an Apple-specific barrier, and whether the fault only occurs when the two threads land on DIFFERENT cluster types (test by pinning cores from ONE cluster only via a c2probe-style DTB); (3) try CONFIG_ARM64_WORKAROUND_* / idle=nop interaction -- we always boot idle=nop because M4 loses CPU state on WFI, which changes the timing of every idle core; (4) bisect a minimal C reproducer (fork + write to a shared page in a loop) so it can be reported upstream without the boot machinery. Check whether yuka/upstream have seen this on t8132; it may be a known M4 erratum. ROUND 1 RESULT 2026-08-03: THRESHOLD = 2 is the limit. maxcpus=1 fully clean; maxcpus=2 runs but the fault still fires on non-init processes (arm64_force_sig_fault -> make_task_dead) so processes randomly die; maxcpus=3/4 kill PID 1 -> panic; 5 hangs. INTRA-CLUSTER HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: dts/t6040-j614s-dcuart-onepercluster.dts gives one CPU per cluster (verified from MPIDRs in the boot log: CPU1 0x0 midr 0x611f0541 E-cluster0, CPU2 0x10200 midr 0x611f0551 P-cluster2) and it STILL panics with the same copy_page fault -- so it is core COUNT, not cluster placement. NON-TEMPORAL hypothesis also refuted: copy_page.S uses plain ldp/stp, no ldnp/stnp. Fault detail: pc copy_page+0x48, lr copy_highpage+0x70, both x0/x1 kernel linear-map, victim gets SIGSEGV. NEXT: minimal C reproducer runnable at maxcpus=2 (where the system survives) to decouple from the boot machinery and make it upstream-reportable; then idle=yield vs idle=nop at maxcpus=3; then CoW cache-maintenance review; then ask upstream whether t8132 shows this. Doc: evidence/2026-08-03-t6040-205-smp-cow-investigation.md ROUND 2 2026-08-03: DEPENDENCY-FREE REPRODUCER built (scripts/t6040-cow-repro.sh, pure busybox: 512 KB shell heap + 300 forking subshells that write to it). CONTROLLED RESULT: maxcpus=2 -> 3 kernel traces, task killed, loop never finishes; maxcpus=1 -> 0 traces, loop completes. Failing path from the reproducer: do_page_fault -> do_bad_area -> die_kernel_fault -> arm64_force_sig_fault -> make_task_dead (die_kernel_fault = fault taken in KERNEL mode). Each data point now costs ~40 s in a live shell instead of a full boot, and the script is directly usable in an upstream report. ALSO: idle=yield HANGS the boot on M4 (clean cmdline, zero kernel output) so the idle-loop hypothesis cannot be tested by swapping idle methods; idle=nop is effectively mandatory. Fixed t6040-boot-dcuart.sh to take BOOT_MAXCPUS/BOOT_IDLE instead of hardcoding them (duplicate cmdline args made the first idle test inconclusive). NEXT: report upstream/yuka; instrument copy_highpage/copy_page with a WARN on the page addresses; audit the Asahi tree for a CoW/cache-maintenance patch missing from this port. ROUND 3 2026-08-03: instrumented copy_highpage with a WARN_ONCE validating copy_page args (alignment, virt_addr_valid, self-copy), verified in the packed Image. RESULT: the WARN NEVER FIRED and the bug DISAPPEARED -- four consecutive reproducer runs at maxcpus=2 all completed with 0 traces, where the un-instrumented build faulted on the first run. So (a) copy_page inputs are always valid -- not a bad-argument bug; (b) a few instructions of work before copy_page suppress the race => Heisenbug, consistent with a MISSING BARRIER or cache maintenance before the CoW copy (virt_addr_valid does pfn/sparsemem reads). Caveat: faulting runs were the build immediately before the instrument commit, so a same-session control of the un-instrumented Image is needed (ticket 208). Next: bisect the minimal suppressing operation (ticket 207). 207 CLOSED 2026-08-03: barrier hypothesis refuted (a plain read suppresses it as well as smp_mb). The race is not in copy_highpage. Redirect to page lifetime/refcount and TLBI completion, and to an upstream report using the reproducer. ROUND 6 2026-08-03: (1) MIXED CORE TYPES REFUTED -- a P-only pair (P00+P01, both Everest, MPIDR-verified) faults and faults HARDER (3 boot traces) than the mixed pair (0). 2x2 with topology verified: P00+E0 diff-cluster/diff-type = 0 boot traces; P00+P10 diff-cluster/same-type = 1; P00+P01 same-cluster/same-type = 3. Cluster sharing is an AGGRAVATING factor, not the cause. NO safe 2-CPU pairing exists. (2) NOT CoW-SPECIFIC: the P-only boot fault is __pi_memcpy_generic <- jbd2_journal_recover <- ext4_fill_super (ext4 journal replay). Three signatures now: copy_page/CoW, __pi_memcpy_generic/ext4-journal, copy_folio_from_iter_atomic/initramfs-unpack. Common factor = ANY BULK MEMCPY with another CPU active. Retire the "CoW bug" framing (and 121s unpack framing). (3) NEW PRIME SUSPECT: secondary-CPU init state. We bring secondaries up via spin-table out of m1n1; if a secondary starts with cache/MMU/MAIR/TCR or Apple-specific SPRR/GXF/APRR state mismatched against the boot CPU, its memory view is incoherent exactly this way -- big copies corrupt, small ones survive. Next (offline): diff m1n1 secondary entry state vs secondary_start_kernel expectations; check the Asahi tree for M4 secondary-boot handling this port lacks. Round 6 addendum: silent-vs-fault data-corruption test (6x 16MiB dd+cp+md5 compare at maxcpus=2 on p2clusters) did NOT complete -- session died before reporting and the machine then showed a fresh SMP boot panicking at 3.74s. INCONCLUSIVE; not attributed to the test. Rerun with per-step output streamed to /dev/kmsg (at maxcpus=2 the shell itself can be the victim, so buffered output is lost). Whether bulk copies corrupt SILENTLY or only fault is still the key open question: silent => coherency bug, fault-only => mapping/lifetime. ROUND 7 2026-08-03 (BIGGEST RESULT YET, but NOT a fix): (1) FOURTH signature clear_page <- __alloc_frozen_pages_noprof <- alloc_pages_mpol <- vma_alloc_folio_noprof -- a pure ZEROING of a newly allocated page, NO copy at all. Unifying factor across all four signatures (copy_page/CoW, __pi_memcpy_generic/ext4-journal, copy_folio_from_iter_atomic/initramfs, clear_page/allocator) is a BULK STORE INTO A FRESHLY ALLOCATED PAGE. Both the "CoW" and "bulk memcpy" framings are superseded. (2) rodata=on (block-mapped linear map instead of the default page-granular rodata=full) changes the failure QUALITATIVELY: maxcpus=5 went from TOTAL HANG (20 lines, zero kernel output, every attempt) to a full boot -- 557 lines, "smp: Brought up 1 node, 5 CPUs", OpenRC starts, NO PANIC. maxcpus=2 also gave 0 traces over 4 reproducer runs. (3) NOT A FIX: at maxcpus=5 one clear_page fault still fires and userspace becomes unresponsive (shell dead, no SSH). DO NOT ship rodata=on or claim 5-core support. maxcpus=1 remains the only clean config. NEXT (cheapest first): init_on_alloc=0/init_on_free=0 (init_on_alloc would explain why clear_page is the signature under allocation pressure); then CONFIG_RODATA_FULL_DEFAULT_ENABLED=n at build time; then instrument set_direct_map_*_noflush and its TLBI broadcast. IRC CORROBORATION 2026-08-02: sven asked yuka "does linux boot without the weird crashes with smp on 26.x or 27 now?" and yuka replied she has not seen "trying to write to read-only" for a few weeks but "it depends very much on the kernel config used". So this is a KNOWN M4 SMP issue (not a Wallace bug), its signature matches our original unpack_to_rootfs fault verbatim, and config-dependence independently corroborates our rodata=full-vs-on result. Config bisect is now ticket 215 and is the top action. THRESHOLD CORRECTED 2026-08-03: with the 8.8 MB sdroot initramfs and baseline config the boundary is maxcpus>=6 (5 boots, 6+ hang) -- the original 121 framing was right. The earlier "2 is the limit" came from the 99 MB image. Five bulk-store signatures now: clear_page, copy_page, __pi_memcpy_generic, copy_folio_from_iter_atomic, __pi_memset_generic. rodata/TLB_RANGE/AFDBM all proven IRRELEVANT (218 round 2). ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-03 via ticket 221: SMC. Disabling smc+smc_mbox alone lets all 14 CPUs boot where the same DTB with SMC hangs 100%. This is NOT a CPU/MMU/cache/TLB bug; the bulk-store faults on freshly allocated pages are the symptom of macsmc disturbing memory as core count rises. All nine earlier rounds of characterisation remain valid as symptom description but the mechanism hypotheses (ordering, barriers, TLB invalidation, page-granular linear map, core type, cluster placement, concurrency) are all superseded. Continue in 221. TWO BUGS CONFIRMED 2026-08-03 (223 round 15): bug A = gP13 (BCM4388 power-on) causes a deterministic pre-console hang at high core counts; bug B = this ticket, bulk-store corruption into freshly allocated pages, intermittent from 2 cores up. Avoiding gP13 (pwren-sd-only DTB) reaches 14 CPUs + SD root + OpenRC and then userspace dies, i.e. B is independent of A and A was masking it. Use pwren-sd-only at maxcpus=14 as the harness for B from now on. ROUND 17 2026-08-03 (pwren-sd-only harness): characterised -- maxcpus=14 boots 14 CPUs but bare shell DEAD; 8 -> 3 traces, shell dead; 4 -> 0 boot traces and shell ALIVE, so maxcpus=4 is the usable interactive harness. KEY FINDING: bug B threshold MOVES WITH WIFI POWER -- with the full DTB (WiFi powered) the limit was 2 cores and the reproducer faulted at 2; with pwren-sd-only (WiFi unpowered) maxcpus=4 boots clean with a live shell. So the BCM4388 being powered aggravates bug B too, not just bug A; "B is independent of A" needs qualifying -- distinct failures, common aggravator. REPRODUCER at 4 cores: 24 traces ALL from run 1, none in runs 2-4, loop completes each time -- the first-touch bias in its clearest form, so ONLY RUN 1 IS INFORMATIVE. Every sampled trace is clear_page (allocator page zeroing). INTEGRITY QUESTION STILL OPEN: a heavier test (3x 2 MiB generate/md5/cp/md5) produced NO result lines and killed the shell while the kernel trace count stayed at 24 -- i.e. the process died with NO kernel fault, which leans towards "processes are killed, not silently corrupted" but proves nothing. Retry with ~64 KiB per iteration so a MATCH/MISMATCH lands before the shell can die. NEW TOOLING RULES: never delete the console log while the reader holds it open (output goes to the unlinked inode and a good boot looks empty); never grep a marker that also appears in the echoed command (match the timestamped form ^\[[ 0-9.]+\] MARKER). ROUND 18 2026-08-03 -- THE INTEGRITY QUESTION IS ANSWERED: BUG B IS FAIL-STOP, NOT SILENT CORRUPTION. Method that finally worked: 64 KiB units (not 2 MiB), generate the pattern ONCE, cmp -s instead of two md5sums (2 forks/iter not 4), a marker after every step, and match results only in the timestamped form. Result 1 (no fault fired): 8x cp+cmp = SAME 8, DIFFER 0, traces 0 -- test is sound. Result 2 (decisive, fresh boot so first-touch available): backgrounded the fork-heavy reproducer and ran 12 cp+cmp verifications in the foreground -> SAME=12, DIFFER=0, verify loop COMPLETED, background load DIED (LOADDONE never printed), 1 kernel fault. So a fault fired, killed the load process, and every one of 12 data verifications in the surviving process was byte-identical. CONSEQUENCE: >1 core is a STABILITY problem, not a DATA-INTEGRITY one -- the persistent SD root is not silently rotting, processes just die. Fits the fault path (die_kernel_fault -> arm64_force_sig_fault -> make_task_dead is fail-stop by construction). SCOPE LIMITS, do not overclaim: this shows no corruption in a SURVIVING process while a fault killed a DIFFERENT process; it does not prove a process hit by the fault never writes bad data before dying, nor that a fault during page-cache writeback cannot reach storage. Those are separate tests. Still fsck after a multi-core crash (ordinary unclean-shutdown risk).
